title: PRPC Overview
learning_objectives: Understand what PRPC (PEGA Rules Process Commander) is
Learn about PRPC architecture and components
Recognize different types of rules in PEGA

introduction.title: Introduction to PRPC
introduction.text: PEGA Rules Process Commander (PRPC) is the foundational platform that powers all PEGA applications. It provides the runtime environment, development tools, and rule-based architecture that makes PEGA's low-code approach possible. Understanding PRPC is essential for anyone working with PEGA applications.

sections.title: What is PRPC?
sections.content: PRPC stands for PEGA Rules Process Commander. It is the core platform that provides the infrastructure for building, deploying, and running PEGA applications. Think of PRPC as the engine that powers all PEGA functionality.
key_points: PRPC is the foundational platform for all PEGA applications
It provides both development and runtime environments
Everything in PEGA is built using rules stored in PRPC
It handles process execution, data management, and user interfaces

sections.title: PRPC Architecture
sections.content: PRPC follows a multi-tier architecture that separates concerns and provides scalability and maintainability.

subsections.title: Presentation Tier
subsections.content: The presentation tier handles all user interface elements and user interactions. This includes web pages, mobile interfaces, and portal components.

subsections.title: Business Logic Tier
subsections.content: This tier contains all the business rules, processes, and decision logic. It's where the core application functionality resides.

subsections.title: Data Tier
subsections.content: The data tier manages all data storage, retrieval, and persistence. It includes both PEGA's internal database and connections to external systems.

sections.title: Rule-Based Development
sections.content: PRPC's core philosophy is that everything is a rule. This rule-based approach is what enables PEGA's low-code development model and makes applications highly maintainable.

key_concepts.description: In PRPC, all application components - from user interfaces to business logic to data structures - are defined as rules stored in the database.
PRPC uses a sophisticated rule resolution algorithm to determine which rule to execute based on context, inheritance, and versioning.
Rules can inherit from other rules, promoting reusability and consistency across applications.
Multiple versions of rules can coexist, allowing for controlled deployment and rollback capabilities.

sections.title: Types of Rules in PRPC
sections.content: PRPC includes many different types of rules, each serving specific purposes in application development.

examples: Flow rules - Define process steps and routing
Activity rules - Define specific processing tasks
Decision rules - Define business decision logic

rule_categories.description: Define how users interact with the application
examples: Harness rules - Define page layouts and structure
Section rules - Define reusable UI components
Control rules - Define individual form controls
Property rules - Define data fields and attributes
Data Page rules - Define reusable data structures
Report Definition rules - Define data queries
Connector rules - Define external service connections
Service rules - Define web service interfaces
Parse rules - Define data transformation logic

sections.title: PRPC Development Environment
sections.content: PRPC provides several development environments tailored for different types of users and development scenarios.

environments.name: App Studio
environments.description: A simplified, low-code development environment designed for business users to create and modify applications with minimal technical knowledge.

environments.name: Dev Studio
environments.description: A comprehensive development environment that provides access to all PEGA capabilities and advanced configuration options.

environments.name: Prediction Studio
environments.description: Specialized environment for creating and managing predictive and adaptive models.

sections.title: PRPC Runtime Environment
sections.content: When applications run, PRPC provides the runtime environment that executes rules, manages data, and handles user interactions.

runtime_features.description: Interprets and executes rules based on the current context and rule resolution algorithm.
Manages case lifecycle, work routing, and process orchestration.
Handles data persistence, caching, and database operations.
Manages connections to external systems and data sources.
Enforces authentication, authorization, and data security policies.

sections.title: Benefits of PRPC Architecture
sections.content: The PRPC architecture provides several key benefits that make PEGA applications powerful and maintainable.

benefits.description: Rule-based development allows for quick application creation and modification without traditional coding.
Rules are stored in a structured format that makes them easy to understand, modify, and maintain.
Rules can be inherited and reused across different applications and contexts.
Multi-tier architecture allows applications to scale horizontally and vertically as needed.
Rule resolution and inheritance provide flexibility to handle different business scenarios.
Built-in versioning and rule management provide strong governance capabilities.

summary.title: Key Takeaways
points: PRPC is the foundational platform that powers all PEGA applications
It follows a multi-tier architecture separating presentation, business logic, and data
Everything in PEGA is defined as rules stored in the database
Rule resolution determines which rules execute based on context
Different development environments serve different user types
The runtime environment executes rules and manages application lifecycle

next_steps.title: What's Next?
next_steps.text: Now that you understand PRPC and its architecture, the next tutorial will guide you through installing and setting up your PEGA development environment.
